what: English 1:1 with two similar male voices (hard for diarization)

turns.text: Hi Tom, welcome. Take a seat anywhere. What would you like to talk about today?
Hi. Well, I've been putting this off for a while. I think I need to talk about the whole move thing.
The move. Tell me what's happening.
I've been offered a job as a physiotherapist at a sports clinic in Dublin, and I have to give them an answer by the end of the month. On paper it's a dream. Better pay, better hours.
But?
But my stomach turns every time I think about it.
What does your stomach say?
That I'm going to mess it up. My girlfriend Sarah has a good job here in Bristol at the hospital, and she doesn't want to move, so it would mean doing long distance.
How does Sarah feel about you going?
She says she'll support whatever I decide. Which is kind, but it's also the worst thing, because then it's all on me.
It sounds like you'd almost rather she told you what to do.
Exactly. Isn't that pathetic?
I wouldn't call it pathetic. It's a big decision.

And on top of that I hate flying, I'm properly scared of it, I haven't been on a plane since a bad turbulence flight to Spain six years ago. Dublin is a forty minute flight. I'd have to do it every month to see her.
Could you go by ferry instead?
I could, and it takes about nine hours, so that's no good.
So the fear of flying is part of the weight.
A big part. I've been lying awake working out how many flights a year. Twelve. Twelve flights.
Have you tried anything for the flying? Any help?
I did a course once. It was a one-day thing at Heathrow, and I got as far as sitting in a simulator and then I walked out.
That took courage, even getting that far.
I suppose. My brother Ian lives in Cork and he keeps telling me to just go, that I'm overthinking everything as always.
What do you make of his advice?
He's probably right. But he's never been anxious a day in his life, so what does he know?
Fair enough. Let's step back. When you imagine saying yes, what do you feel?
Relief for about ten seconds. Then dread.
And saying no?
Relief for about ten seconds. Then regret. It's the same, just in reverse.
That's very honest. So the answer may not be in the feelings alone.
No. I don't take any medication for the anxiety, the doctor suggested it but I'd rather try talking first.
Understood. Then let's try something practical. What would a week in Dublin look like? Write down the real details, the commute, the flat, the clinic.
I can do that. I visited the clinic last month, actually. They were really welcoming.
Good. Then maybe go back for another visit, and treat that as a test flight.
Ha. A test flight. That's actually not bad.
Shall we meet again next week, before your deadline?
Yes please. I'll bring the list.
